interactions.label: A district health officer notices that TB cure rates vary widely across PHCs in

params.question: A district health officer notices that TB cure rates vary widely across PHCs in her district, with different physicians using different treatment durations. Which structural feature of national health programmes is specifically designed to prevent this kind of variation?

answers.text: Dedicated supply chains ensuring programme medicines are consistently available

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Dedicated supply chains ensure medicines like MDT blister packs or DOTS medicines reach PHCs reliably, but they do not address variation in how physicians prescribe or manage treatment duration.

answers.text: Programme-specific training for health workers in specialised skills

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Training equips workers with skills like reading slit skin smears or supervising DOTS, but it is the standardised protocol — not training alone — that eliminates variation in treatment regimens across centres.

answers.text: Standardised treatment protocols that remove variation as a source of failure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. A standardised regimen like NTEP's six-month daily course removes individual physician variation by providing one uniform protocol for all PHCs, so cure rates depend on adherence rather than on each physician's personal approach.

answers.text: Programme accountability through clear targets and monitoring indicators

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Accountability measures like treatment success rate targets help identify underperforming centres, but they detect variation after it occurs rather than prevent it. The standardised protocol is what removes variation at source.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the four reasons national health programmes exist. The specific feature that eliminates variation in treatment is the standardised protocol, such as NTEP's uniform six-month regimen applied across all PHCs.
Exactly right. Standardised protocols are the structural solution to treatment variation — they replace fifty different physician approaches with one evidence-based regimen.

params.question: Under the current National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme, sputum smear microscopy is the primary diagnostic test, with CBNAAT/TrueNAT reserved as a backup.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Under the current NTEP, this hierarchy has been reversed. CBNAAT or TrueNAT is now the primary diagnostic test, providing rapid results and simultaneous rifampicin resistance detection. Sputum smear microscopy serves as the backup, not the first-line investigation.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — the hierarchy is reversed. Under the current NTEP, CBNAAT or TrueNAT is the primary diagnostic tool, offering rapid molecular detection and simultaneous rifampicin resistance testing. Sputum smear microscopy now serves only as a backup when molecular testing is unavailable.

interactions.label: In a district where private practitioners deliver most first-contact care, the I

params.question: In a district where private practitioners deliver most first-contact care, the IDSP reports show very low disease incidence despite neighbouring districts reporting active outbreaks. Which level of surveillance failure most likely explains this discrepancy?

answers.text: Data quality problems causing miscoded diagnoses at public reporting facilities

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Miscoded diagnoses would distort disease classification — labelling cholera as ordinary diarrhoea, for example — but would not produce uniformly low overall incidence. Cases would still appear in the system, just under the wrong codes.

answers.text: Underreporting because private providers have no formal reporting obligation to the surveillance system

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Private providers deliver most first-contact care in India but have no obligation to report to the public surveillance system. When most illness is managed privately, a huge share never enters the formal reporting chain, producing artificially low incidence figures.

answers.text: Infrastructure gaps with patchy internet preventing timely data upload from PHCs

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Internet connectivity issues would delay data from public facilities, not systematically produce low incidence in a district where the private sector handles most patient encounters. The issue is structural — cases never enter the system at all.

answers.text: Health worker knowledge gaps preventing ASHAs from recognising epidemic-prone syndromes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: ASHA knowledge gaps would reduce case detection within the public system, but the scenario highlights that private practitioners handle most care. The low incidence reflects the private sector's invisibility to surveillance, not public-sector detection failure.

overallFeedback.feedback: Consider which failure mechanism would make most illness invisible when private practitioners handle the majority of patient encounters. The key issue is structural: private providers are not part of the reporting chain.
Well analysed. When the private sector delivers most care but has no reporting obligation, the surveillance system sees only a fraction of the true disease burden.

interactions.label: During a cholera outbreak investigation in a village, the team has verified the

params.question: During a cholera outbreak investigation in a village, the team has verified the diagnosis, confirmed the outbreak exceeds baseline, and identified contaminated well water as the likely source. A colleague argues they must complete all remaining investigation steps before implementing control measures. What is the correct approach?

answers.text: Complete the case-control study first to statistically confirm the water source before acting

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Waiting for a formal case-control study before acting on a probable source delays intervention and allows continued transmission. Statistical confirmation strengthens the evidence but is not a prerequisite for initiating control.

answers.text: Halt the investigation entirely and redirect all resources to water decontamination

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Stopping the investigation means losing the chance to identify additional sources, missed cases, or secondary transmission routes that could sustain the outbreak. Investigation and control must proceed simultaneously.

answers.text: Wait for the final outbreak report before notifying the district health authority

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Delaying notification until a final report is ready wastes critical response time. The Epidemic Diseases Act supports immediate action and notification on reasonable evidence, not after all steps are complete.

answers.text: Implement control measures immediately while continuing the investigation in parallel

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The outbreak investigation framework explicitly states that control measures begin as soon as there is reasonable evidence, running in parallel with remaining investigation steps — not sequentially after all steps are complete.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the key principle of outbreak investigation: control measures start as soon as there is reasonable evidence, running in parallel with remaining steps. You do not wait to finish all ten steps before acting.
Exactly right. A confirmed probable source is sufficient to start control while the investigation continues. Investigation and control are parallel, not sequential.

interactions.label: An ASHA worker in a rural sub-centre encounters a 10-year-old child who develope

params.question: An ASHA worker in a rural sub-centre encounters a 10-year-old child who developed sudden weakness in both legs overnight. According to her training under the National Health Mission, what should she do?

answers.text: Immediately call the PHC medical officer, as this syndrome requires urgent escalation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Sudden weakness in a child under fifteen is the hallmark presentation of acute flaccid paralysis, one of the syndromes requiring immediate notification to the PHC medical officer — not routine weekly reporting via the S-form.

answers.text: Record the case in the weekly S-form and submit it at the next scheduled reporting date

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Acute flaccid paralysis is explicitly listed among conditions that must NOT wait for the weekly S-form. The escalation rule requires an immediate call to the PHC medical officer for AFP, cholera, and unexplained deaths.

answers.text: Start oral rehydration therapy and observe the child for 48 hours before reporting

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Oral rehydration is irrelevant for sudden limb weakness, and a 48-hour observation delay would critically compromise polio surveillance. AFP demands immediate notification, not a watch-and-wait approach.

answers.text: Refer the child directly to the district hospital without informing the PHC medical officer

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While referral may eventually be needed, the PHC medical officer must be notified first so the surveillance reporting chain is activated. Bypassing the PHC breaks the pathway that triggers polio surveillance at district and national levels.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the escalation rule: acute flaccid paralysis, cholera, and unexplained deaths require an immediate call to the PHC medical officer, not routine weekly reporting through the S-form.
Well done. AFP in any child under 15 demands immediate escalation to the PHC medical officer — this is a cornerstone of India's polio surveillance system.
